belief: Being afraid of death means my faith is weak.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that being afraid of death means your faith is weak, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Hearing that Christians should welcome death without fear. Anxiety about dying, illness, or the unknown. Comparing yourself with people who seem peaceful about death. Painful experiences of watching someone die. Health scares that bring fear to the surface.
teaches: Death is an enemy, and it is natural to feel fear about it. Even Jesus was deeply troubled before His death. Scripture says Christ shared our humanity to free those who all their lives were held in slavery by the fear of death. Fear of death is something He came to heal, not something He condemns. He has prepared a place for you, and through Him death has lost its sting.
self_statements: If I had real faith, I wouldn’t be afraid to die.
My fear proves I’m not sure of heaven.
Good Christians are excited to die.
I can’t admit this fear to anyone.
My fear must mean I’m not saved.
errors: Believing you must either have no fear or weak faith.
“I should never be afraid of death.”
Concluding “I feel afraid, so my faith must be weak.”
Comparing your feelings to others’ apparent calm.
questions: Why did Christ share our humanity, according to Hebrews 2:15?
Was Jesus troubled before His death?
Does Scripture call death a friend or an enemy?
What has Jesus prepared for me?
What does 1 Corinthians 15 say has happened to death’s sting?
Is my fear about death itself, about pain, or about leaving people?
Can I bring this fear to Jesus and let Him comfort me?
truth: Being afraid of death does not mean my faith is weak. Death is an enemy, and Jesus came to free people from the fear of it. He has prepared a place for me and has taken away death’s sting. I can bring my fear to Him, and He will comfort me as I walk through the valley.
hw_questions: Why did Christ share our humanity?
Was Jesus troubled before His death?
Is death a friend or an enemy?
What has Jesus prepared for me?
What exactly am I afraid of?
hw_truths: Fear of death does not mean weak faith.
Jesus came to free me from the fear of death.
Jesus has prepared a place for me.
God is with me in the valley.
Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
log: When fear of death comes, write it down and answer it with one promise from Jesus.
name_example: Even though Sarah walks through the valley of the shadow of death, she will fear no evil, for You are with her; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort her.
actions: Write down exactly what you fear about death,
and next to each fear write a promise of God.
Read John 14:1–6 each night this week
Talk honestly with a pastor or mature believer
talk with your doctor or a Christian counselor.
tracker: One fear I answered with a promise
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You came to free me from the fear of death. Help me reject the lie that being afraid means my faith is weak. When I am afraid, comfort me with Your presence and Your promises. Thank You for the place You are preparing for me. In Your name, Amen.
